method: Compared the remaining exact-title OpenAlex/repository clusters with official university repository metadata and specialist bibliographies. Repository and OpenAlex discovery rows are retained as metadata with replacement pointers; canonical work records retain the actual article or chapter type.

entries.finding: Ghent University's Academic Bibliography identifies one 1978 Bibliotheca Orientalis 35 article by Klaas Smelik, pages 174-177, with handle 1854/LU-378915. The only deposited file is a published-version PDF restricted to UGent users and the record supplies no abstract. SRC-589994C2222B is the canonical article; SRC-D7DD2C56A96B is the OpenAlex discovery row for the same work.
entries.scope_disposition: Left unclassified: the accessible record verifies bibliographic identity but does not describe the article's contents beyond its title.

entries.finding: The University of Milano-Bicocca record identifies one 2005 Journal of the Academy of Sciences - Syriac Commission 21 article, pages 31-46, and marks the version-of-record file reserved. The Comprehensive Bibliography on Syriac Studies and Mnamon both supply the fuller authorship, Yusef Matti Quzi and Ali H. Faraj; Faraj's university CV supplies Academy of Sciences Press, Baghdad. SRC-E689BC4C3787 is the canonical article; SRC-FD7C9081F047 is the OpenAlex discovery row for the same work.
entries.scope_disposition: Left unclassified: the accessible records verify title, authorship, publication and language metadata but provide no abstract or inspected text.

entries.finding: Southampton's public OAI-PMH record identifies one peer-reviewed book section by Dan Levene, dated 2010, in Ada Rapoport-Albert's edited volume Late Aramaic: The Literary and Linguistic Context of the Zohar, with publication status 'In Press' and no deposited full text. SRC-C40FB2ED8EE8 is the canonical chapter; SRC-479F50E73B60 is the OpenAlex discovery row for the same work.
entries.scope_disposition: Left unclassified: the official record contains no abstract or full text, and the title alone is not being used to infer an edition scope.

policy: These findings repair bibliographic identity only. They do not validate object authenticity or provenance, resolve bowl identities, certify a reading, infer a work scope from its title, or grant permission to reproduce protected text or images.
